claim: subject follows a path/spline driven by scroll position

q1_defects.answer: No defects. Card travels across the frame and banks cleanly; chrome sharp at DPR-2. The metrics effHue 280-318 on control frames is hue-noise on a near-neutral panel (effSat 0.02-0.03), NOT a purple tint — the rendered card reads as the standard graphite/brass palette.
evidence: metrics: control-bank-low effSat 0.03 effHue 280 is noise on near-black, panel is neutral graphite

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads as a card following a curved spline with banking: idle=card lower-left banked left with glowing brass header, play-1=moved up-left at a new angle, play-3=upper-right banked the other way. It travels along a path and rolls into the curves. Full card chrome preserved, matches ground truth.

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. bank control clearly increases the roll/tilt as the card moves through the curve (low near-level, high ~20 deg bank); travel control shifts how far along the path the card sits at the pinned point. Both produce visible changes.

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive: large position/orientation deltas across play frames, frameDeltaMag 21.5 then 21.9 then 13.9; controls apply ~571-587ms.

q5_net.answer: PLEASED — the card clearly flies along a curved path and banks like a plane through a turn; the full card look is kept throughout and both knobs read.

flags.note: travel control is subtler than bank (changedFrac 0.1679 but the two poses are close); reads as a smaller path-offset shift than a user might expect from a 'travel' label.
flags.evidence: control: travel low vs high effRGB ~44 both, changedFrac 0.1679
